metadata.title: AI Foundations Information Theory — Sources
metadata.description: Primary papers and references for 11 information-theory primitives: Shannon entropy, mutual information, KL divergence, cross-entropy, channel capacity, rate-distortion, MDL, information bottleneck, Fano's inequality, AEP, and redundancy/compression.

research_papers.name: Shannon: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
research_papers.description: Shannon, C. E. (1948). Bell System Technical Journal, 27(3), 379–423. Foundational paper introducing entropy, channel capacity, source coding theorem, and channel coding theorem. Primary source for primitives #1, #5, #10.

research_papers.name: Cover & Thomas: Elements of Information Theory, 2nd ed.
research_papers.description: Cover, T. M. & Thomas, J. A. (2006). Wiley. Canonical textbook reference for all 11 primitives. Entropy (Ch.2), AEP (Ch.3), rate-distortion (Ch.10), MDL (Ch.14).

research_papers.name: MacKay: Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms
research_papers.description: MacKay, D. J. C. (2003). Cambridge University Press. Free online. Covers all primitives with worked examples. Entropy (Ch.2), source coding (Ch.5–6), channel capacity (Ch.9–11), IB-adjacent material (Ch.28).

research_papers.name: Tishby, Pereira & Bialek: The Information Bottleneck Method
research_papers.description: Tishby, N., Pereira, F. C. & Bialek, W. (2000). arXiv:physics/0004057. Original information bottleneck paper. Self-consistency equations, IB curve, Lagrangian formulation. Primary source for primitive #8.

research_papers.name: Tishby & Schwartz-Ziv: Opening the Black Box via Information
research_papers.description: Tishby, N. & Schwartz-Ziv, R. (2017). arXiv:1703.00810. IB interpretation of deep neural network layers — fitting and compression phases. Source for primitive #8 (deep learning view).

research_papers.name: Saxe et al.: On the Information Bottleneck Theory of Deep Learning
research_papers.description: Saxe, A. M. et al. (2018). ICLR 2019. Rebuttal to Tishby/Schwartz-Ziv: compression phase depends on activation function and MI estimator; does not generalize. Critical for IB anti-pattern guidance in primitive #8.

research_papers.name: Alemi et al.: Deep Variational Information Bottleneck
research_papers.description: Alemi, A. A. et al. (2017). ICLR 2017. Variational IB (VIB) for high-dimensional data; gradient-based optimization via ELBO-style bound. Source for primitive #8 (variational IB).

research_papers.name: Rissanen: Modeling by Shortest Data Description
research_papers.description: Rissanen, J. (1978). Automatica, 14(5), 465–471. Original MDL paper. Two-part code: L(model) + L(data|model). Primary source for primitive #7.

research_papers.name: Grünwald: The Minimum Description Length Principle
research_papers.description: Grünwald, P. (2007). MIT Press. Comprehensive MDL reference: two-part codes, NML, refined MDL, stochastic complexity, Bayesian connection. Primary source for primitive #7.

research_papers.name: Belghazi et al.: MINE — Mutual Information Neural Estimation
research_papers.description: Belghazi, M. I. et al. (2018). ICML 2018. Neural lower bound on MI using Donsker-Varadhan representation. Enables MI estimation in high-dimensional continuous spaces. Source for primitive #2 (continuous MI estimation).

research_papers.name: Paninski: Estimation of Entropy and Mutual Information
research_papers.description: Paninski, L. (2003). Neural Computation, 15(6), 1191–1253. Bias-variance analysis of plug-in entropy and MI estimators; conditions for consistent estimation. Source for primitive #2 failure modes.

research_papers.name: Kraskov, Stögbauer & Grassberger: Estimating Mutual Information
research_papers.description: Kraskov, A., Stögbauer, H. & Grassberger, P. (2004). Physical Review E, 69(6). k-NN based MI estimator for continuous random variables; widely used in neuroscience and ML. Source for primitive #2.

research_papers.name: Kullback & Leibler: On Information and Sufficiency
research_papers.description: Kullback, S. & Leibler, R. A. (1951). Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 22(1), 79–86. Original KL divergence paper. Primary source for primitive #3.

research_papers.name: Lin: Divergence Measures Based on the Shannon Entropy
research_papers.description: Lin, J. (1991). IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 37(1), 145–151. Introduces Jensen-Shannon divergence as a symmetric, bounded divergence. Source for primitive #3 (JS divergence).

research_papers.name: Fano: Transmission of Information
research_papers.description: Fano, R. M. (1961). MIT Press. Original derivation of Fano's inequality and its application to channel coding converse. Primary source for primitive #9.

research_papers.name: Blahut: Computation of Channel Capacity and Rate-Distortion Functions
research_papers.description: Blahut, R. E. (1972). IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 18(4), 460–473. Blahut-Arimoto algorithm for computing R(D) and C numerically. Source for primitives #5, #6.

research_papers.name: Shannon: Coding Theorems for a Discrete Source with a Fidelity Criterion
research_papers.description: Shannon, C. E. (1959). IRE National Convention Record, part 4, 142–163. Original rate-distortion theorem. Primary source for primitive #6.

research_papers.name: Huffman: A Method for the Construction of Minimum-Redundancy Codes
research_papers.description: Huffman, D. A. (1952). Proceedings of the IRE, 40(9), 1098–1101. Huffman coding algorithm. Source for primitive #11.

research_papers.name: Ziv & Lempel: A Universal Algorithm for Sequential Data Compression (LZ77)
research_papers.description: Ziv, J. & Lempel, A. (1977). IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 23(3), 337–343. LZ77 algorithm; basis for zlib, DEFLATE, gzip. Source for primitive #11.

research_papers.name: Ziv & Lempel: Compression of Individual Sequences via Variable-Rate Coding (LZ78)
research_papers.description: Ziv, J. & Lempel, A. (1978). IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 24(5), 530–536. LZ78 algorithm; basis for LZW, GIF. Source for primitive #11.

research_papers.name: Cilibrasi & Vitányi: Clustering by Compression
research_papers.description: Cilibrasi, R. & Vitányi, P. M. B. (2005). IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 51(4), 1523–1545. Normalized Compression Distance (NCD) for parameter-free similarity. Source for primitive #11.

research_papers.name: Polyanskiy, Poor & Verdú: Channel Coding Rate in the Finite Blocklength Regime
research_papers.description: Polyanskiy, Y., Poor, H. V. & Verdú, S. (2010). IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 56(5), 2307–2359. Finite blocklength converse and achievability bounds. Source for primitives #5, #10 (practical rate gap).

research_papers.name: Witten, Neal & Cleary: Arithmetic Coding for Data Compression
research_papers.description: Witten, I. H., Neal, R. M. & Cleary, J. G. (1987). Communications of the ACM, 30(6), 520–540. Practical arithmetic coding. Source for primitive #11.

research_papers.name: McMillan: The Basic Theorems of Information Theory
research_papers.description: McMillan, B. (1953). Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 24(2), 196–219. AEP for stationary ergodic processes; extends Shannon's i.i.d. result. Source for primitive #10.

research_papers.name: Rissanen: Fisher Information and Stochastic Complexity
research_papers.description: Rissanen, J. (1996). IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 42(1), 40–47. Stochastic complexity and the NML code. Source for primitive #7 (refined MDL).

research_papers.name: Müller et al.: When Does Label Smoothing Help?
research_papers.description: Müller, R. et al. (2019). NeurIPS 2019. Analysis of label smoothing as a form of soft cross-entropy target; shows effect on calibration and knowledge distillation. Source for primitive #4 (one-hot label limitation).

research_papers.name: Yoran et al.: The KoLMogorov Test: Compression by Code Generation
research_papers.description: Yoran, O., Zheng, K., Gloeckle, F., Gehring, J., Synnaeve, G. & Cohen, T. (2025). ICLR 2025. Kolmogorov-complexity benchmark for code-generating LLMs: model must produce shortest program that outputs a given sequence. Shows GPT-4o and Llama-3.1-405B perform poorly; synthetic-data gains do not generalise to real data. Grounds compression as a rigorous, contamination-proof intelligence metric. Relevant to primitives #7, #11.

research_papers.name: Niu et al.: Rate-Distortion-Perception Trade-Off in Information Theory, Generative Models, and Intelligent Communications
research_papers.description: Niu, X., Bai, B., Guo, N., Zhang, W. & Han, W. (2025). Entropy, 27(4), 373. Peer-reviewed survey/theory extending rate-distortion with a perceptual constraint: proves high perceptual fidelity strictly raises the minimum rate; derives the information RDP (I-RDP) function; covers KL, TV, and Wasserstein divergence as perception measures. Relevant to primitives #3, #6.

research_papers.name: Lei, Hassani & Bidokhti: Optimal Neural Compressors for the Rate-Distortion-Perception Tradeoff
research_papers.description: Lei, E., Hassani, H. & Bidokhti, S. S. (2025). NeurIPS 2025. Proposes lattice-based neural compressors optimal for the RDP tradeoff; shared dithering provides common randomness; empirically validated on synthetic and real data. Applied complement to RDPEntropy2025. Relevant to primitive #6.

research_papers.name: Abdelaleem, Martini & Nemenman: Accurate Estimation of Mutual Information in High Dimensional Data
research_papers.description: Abdelaleem, E., Martini, K. M. & Nemenman, I. (2025). arXiv:2506.00330 (stat.ML). Practical protocol for reliable neural MI estimation: confidence intervals, consistency checks, probabilistic critics for high-MI regimes. Identifies when neural estimators fail (no accepted tests) and when they succeed (low-dimensional latent dependence, sufficient N). Extends existing MINE/NWJ failure-mode guidance in primitive #2.

research_papers.name: Ni & Lotz: A Neural Difference-of-Entropies Estimator for Mutual Information
research_papers.description: Ni, H. & Lotz, M. (2025). arXiv:2502.13085 (stat.ML). Normalizing-flow-based MI estimator using block autoregressive conditional density parameterisation; improved bias-variance trade-offs on standard benchmarks across 17 experiments. Addresses the high-dimensional MI estimation failure mode in primitive #2.

research_papers.name: Zhu et al.: Narrowing Information Bottleneck Theory for Multimodal Image-Text Representations Interpretability
research_papers.description: Zhu, Z., Jin, Z., Zhang, J., Yang, N., Huang, J., Zhou, J. & Chen, F. (2025). ICLR 2025. Reformulates IB for multimodal (CLIP) settings: eliminates randomness and hyperparameter dependency of standard IB; satisfies attribution axioms; introduces negative property concept. Code: https://github.com/LMBTough/NIB. +9% image, +59% text interpretability vs. baselines. Extends primitive #8 to multimodal regime.

research_papers.name: Cross-modal Information Bottleneck Regularization for Robust CLIP Generalization
research_papers.description: CIBR (2025). ICANN 2025. Interprets CLIP contrastive objective as implicit IB optimization maximising shared cross-modal information while discarding modality-specific redundancy; adds explicit IB regularization (CIBR) yielding superior zero-shot and retrieval performance. Independent corroboration for IB in multimodal learning. Relevant to primitive #8.

research_papers.name: Letizia, Novello & Tonello: Mutual Information Estimation via f-Divergence and Data Derangements
research_papers.description: Letizia, N. A., Novello, N. & Tonello, A. M. (2024). NeurIPS 2024. Proposes f-DIME: discriminative MI estimators based on f-divergence variational representation with derangement architecture; removes the log(K) upper-bound artefact present in InfoNCE/contrastive estimators; achieves excellent bias/variance trade-off at lower complexity than MINE/NWJ. Code: https://github.com/tonellolab/fDIME. Verified: title, authors, NeurIPS 2024 venue, and code repo confirmed via primary URL 2026-05-17. Addresses InfoNCE ceiling bias anti-pattern for primitive #2.

research_papers.name: Hellström, Durisi, Guedj & Raginsky: Generalization Bounds — Perspectives from Information Theory and PAC-Bayes
research_papers.description: Hellström, F., Durisi, G., Guedj, B. & Raginsky, M. (2023/2024). arXiv:2309.04381 (cs.LG), 228-page monograph, v2 revised March 2024. Unifies PAC-Bayesian and information-theoretic generalization bounds under the conditional mutual information (CMI) framework; shows modular proof structure; derives tighter bounds for deep learning by conditioning on training algorithm trajectory. Evidence grade B: large monograph widely cited but arXiv preprint only — no journal or book publication confirmed via primary URL 2026-05-17. Relevant to IT Generalization Bounds theory area and primitive #2.

research_papers.name: Westphal, Hailes & Musolesi: A Generalized Information Bottleneck Theory of Deep Learning
research_papers.description: Westphal, C., Hailes, S. & Musolesi, M. (2025/2026). arXiv:2509.26327 (cs.LG/cs.IT), submitted September 2025, revised January 2026. Reformulates IB using synergistic information (joint-only information via average interaction information); demonstrates compression phases in ReLU networks and Transformers where standard IB fails (Saxe et al. criterion). GIB upper-bounds standard IB under perfect estimation. Evidence grade C: preprint only, no peer-review confirmation as of 2026-05-17. Treat as a promising candidate, not established practice. Relevant to primitive #8.

research_papers.name: Radio: Rate-Distortion Optimization for Large Language Model Compression
research_papers.description: Radio (2025). ICML 2025. Applies rate-distortion theory directly to LLM weight quantization: formulates per-layer bit allocation as an R(D) optimization, introduces a stochastic numerical solver, and shows that scalar quantization is suboptimal — block/vector quantization yields lower distortion at equal bitrate. Demonstrates the practical value of R(D) framework for model compression. Relevant to primitive #6, #7.

research_papers.name: Peng et al.: Flatness-Leveraging Information-Theoretic Generalization Bounds
research_papers.description: Peng et al. (2025/2026). ICLR 2025 (note: submitted January 4, 2026; year discrepancy may reflect ICLR 2026 labeling — venue confirmed as ICLR, exact year unresolved per audit). Derives IT generalization bounds incorporating loss-landscape flatness; 'numerically much tighter' than prior IT bounds; improves Ω(1) to O(1/√n) rate for gradient descent on convex-Lipschitz problems using omniscient trajectory technique. Builds on Hellström et al. CMI framework (HellstromGenBounds2024). Evidence grade B: ICLR conference paper; venue confirmed. Relevant to IT Generalization Bounds theory area.

research_papers.name: Farquhar, Kossen, Kuhn & Gal: Detecting Hallucinations in Large Language Models Using Semantic Entropy
research_papers.description: Farquhar, S., Kossen, J., Kuhn, L. & Gal, Y. (2024). Nature, 630, 625-630. Computes entropy over clusters of semantically equivalent generations (bidirectional NLI entailment) rather than over tokens, making the estimate invariant to paraphrase. Detects confabulations — arbitrary, sampling-unstable answers — without ground-truth labels or task-specific training. Scope limit: blind to consistently-stated false beliefs, since sampling-based measures detect instability, not wrongness. Peer-reviewed; the strongest applied use of primitive #1 in LLM practice. Verified via Nature DOI landing page 2026-08-14 (full text paywalled; citation confirmed via arXiv:2406.15927 which cites it directly).

research_papers.name: Kossen et al.: Semantic Entropy Probes — Robust and Cheap Hallucination Detection in LLMs
research_papers.description: Kossen, J., Han, J., Razzak, M., Schut, L., Malik, S. & Gal, Y. (2024). arXiv:2406.15927 (cs.LG), submitted 22 June 2024. Approximates semantic entropy directly from the hidden states of a single generation, removing the 5-10x sampling overhead of the Nature 2024 method. Makes semantic-entropy gating viable under production latency budgets. Evidence grade B: arXiv preprint, but by the same group as the Nature paper and widely reproduced. Extends primitive #1. Verified via primary URL 2026-08-14.

research_papers.name: Cui et al.: The Entropy Mechanism of Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Language Models
research_papers.description: Cui, G. et al. (2025). arXiv:2505.22617 (cs.LG), submitted 28 May 2025. Establishes the empirical law R = -a*e^H + b linking policy entropy H to downstream reward R in RLVR: performance is traded from entropy, and the ceiling is reached as entropy approaches zero. Over 95% of the entropy drop and most of the gain occur early in training. Identifies tokens with high covariance between log-probability and advantage as the drivers of collapse, and proposes Clip-Cov (restrict updates on those tokens) and KL-Cov (KL-penalise them) as targeted mitigations superior to a blanket entropy bonus. Caveat: the fitted constants a and b are setup-specific and must be refit, though the qualitative law replicates widely. Grounds primitive #1 applied to RL post-training. Verified via primary URL 2026-08-14.

research_papers.name: Huang et al.: Compression Represents Intelligence Linearly
research_papers.description: Huang, Y. et al. (2024). COLM 2024, arXiv:2404.09937. Evaluates 30 public LLMs across 12 benchmarks spanning knowledge/commonsense, coding, and mathematical reasoning; finds downstream benchmark score correlates near-linearly with corpus compression efficiency, Pearson r about -0.95 per domain. Uses bits-per-character rather than bits-per-token precisely because tokenizers differ. Establishes BPC as a cheap, contamination-resistant evaluation proxy. Pairs with KoLMogorovTest2025 as the positive half of the compression-intelligence question: average-case compression tracks capability, worst-case (shortest-program) compression does not. Code: https://github.com/hkust-nlp/llm-compression-intelligence. Relevant to primitives #4, #11. Verified via primary URL 2026-08-14.

research_papers.name: Farooq & Iqbal: Bandwidth-Efficient Multi-Agent Communication through Information Bottleneck and Vector Quantization
research_papers.description: Farooq, A. & Iqbal, K. (2026). IEEE ICRA 2026, arXiv:2602.02035, submitted 2 February 2026. Combines an information-bottleneck objective with vector quantization and a learned gating mechanism deciding when to communicate at all; reports 181.8% performance gain over a no-communication baseline at 71.4% lower bandwidth (800 vs 2800 bits/episode). Targeted at robotic swarms and distributed sensor networks, but the framing transfers directly to LLM agent handoffs and KV-cache passing: budget the message by task-relevant information, not token count. Evidence grade B: accepted conference paper, camera-ready. Relevant to primitives #6, #8.
